'''John Challifour''' (June 13, 1938 – November 27, 2021)<ref name=indiana.edu>{{cite web  | title=In Memoriam: John Challifour | url=https://math.indiana.edu/about/inmemoriam/Challifour,%20J.pdf| access-date=2023-11-19}}</ref> was a professor of mathematical physics at [[Indiana University Bloomington|Indiana University]]'s [[Bloomington, Indiana|Bloomington]] campus.  He was known{{citation needed|date=July 2014}} among the math students of the university for his wry sense of humor and clear teaching style.

He was British-born (Bristol, 1938) but studied in the U. S. (Cincinnati), taking his bachelors (with highest honors) at [[University of California, Berkeley|Berkeley]], before earning his PhD from [[University of Cambridge|Cambridge University]] in 1963.  He taught in [[Boston]] ([[Brandeis University|Brandeis]]) and at [[Princeton University]] before moving to Bloomington with his wife, who works in the [[linguistics]] department at Indiana University.  He died at home on 27 November 2021.

== Research ==
* Generalized functions and Fourier analysis: An introduction (1972). New York: W. A. Benjamin.
* Self-adjointness of lattice Yang-Mills Hamiltonians and Kato's inequality with indefinite metric. Annales de l'institut Henri Poincaré (A) Physique théorique, 42 no. 1 (1985), p.&nbsp;1-15
* with Steven P. Slinker. Euclidean field theory: I. The moment problem.  Comm. Math. Phys.  43, no. 1 (1975), 41–58 [http://projecteuclid.org/Dienst/UI/1.0/Summarize/euclid.cmp/1103899094]
* with R.J. Eden.  Regge Surfaces and Singularities in a Relativistic Theory.   Phys. Rev. 129, 2349–2353 (1963). Issue 5 – 1 March 1963 [https://journals.aps.org/pr/abstract/10.1103/PhysRev.129.2349]
